title: Generator formula for the concrete coefficient mate
statement: Let $f:X\to T$, $F\in\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, $U\subseteq T$, $Y=f^{-1}U$, $Z\subseteq Y$, $g:T'\to U$, $g':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to T'$ satisfy $g'f=f'gU.\iota$, and put $W=g'^{-1}(Y.\iota(Z))$. Use [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pc-module-pullback] and [def-pc-finite-affine-cech-model]. Let $k$ be the explicit linear section map of [lem-pc-coefficient-section-map-linear], and let $q$ be its mate under the composition of tilde/Gamma, pullback/pushforward for $U.\mathrm{toSpecGamma}$, and pullback/pushforward for $g$. For every $s\in F|_Y(Z)$, form its generator using tilde.toOpen and these two pullback units, restricting each inverse-image full open to the full open. Then $q$ on that generator, followed by support identification, equals the restriction to $W\cap f'^{-1}(T')$ of the pullback unit for $g'$ applied to the corresponding section of $F(Y.\iota(Z))$. This asserts a formula for the explicitly constructed mate, not existence of a normalized family.

source.place: Tag 02KE, termwise Cech map; Tag 01I6, Lemma 26.7.1; Tags 0096 and 0097, module adjunction and composition

proof.text:
Apply the hom equivalence of the composed tilde/Gamma and two pullback
adjunctions to the defining mate. Equiv.apply_symm_apply gives the original
linear section map. Expand the composed unit: its components are tilde.toOpen,
then the unit for U.toSpecGamma and the unit for g. Naturality of the second
unit moves the first full-open restriction past it; naturality of the mate
moves the last restriction past the mate. The two resulting restrictions on
the target, followed by the support identification, compose to restriction
from the inverse-image support to W intersect fprime inverse image top.
Expand the original linear section map and combine its restriction with this
one by functoriality. This is precisely the pullback-unit section restricted
through hW and then to the displayed intersection. Proof irrelevance identifies
all inclusion and equality morphisms. No affine or cartesian hypothesis is used.
